first_impression.reaction: Our daughter has her heart set on Santorini and sent me this. The opening says these packages share a name and very little else, and that rooms, food and drink are where they part ways. That is where our money goes, so yes, I'm reading it properly, top to bottom.

journey.quote: Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights, music times and currency before paying a deposit that may not be refundable.
journey.reaction: A deposit that may not be refundable. Thank you. That's the first thing I'd want her to know, and it's right at the top.

journey.quote: Several Santorini venues require a wedding planner on top of the venue fee, which changes what a package is really worth to you.
journey.reaction: So there's another person to pay on top of the venue. Better I hear that now than when the invoice arrives.

journey.section: Ceremony space, set-up and a coordinator
journey.quote: Each includes the altar table, chandelier, lanterns with candles, Tiffany chairs, a sound system, round or rectangular tables, linen, plating, cutlery, accessible facilities, an air-conditioned bridal room, in-house catering facilities and a bar.
journey.reaction: On the iPad this is a wall of chairs and chandeliers. That's my daughter's department. I did notice 'accessible facilities' tucked in the middle, which is the only bit I care about, and I nearly missed it.

journey.section: Ceremony space, set-up and a coordinator
journey.quote: Music is capped at 60 dB until 11.30pm.
journey.reaction: 60 dB, 70 dB, 80 dB further down. I have no idea what that means in real life. Is that a quiet dinner or can people dance?

journey.section: Reception, menus and drinks where the venue states them
journey.quote: Open bar packages are optional, but once chosen they apply to every adult guest.
journey.reaction: That's the kind of clause that catches you. Half our side doesn't drink. Good to have it spelled out.

journey.section: Packages for two, elopements and small weddings
journey.quote: Kapari Natural Resort in Imerovigli accepts events for up to about 30 people, and provides a dedicated wedding planner who works with the hotel team.
journey.reaction: By now I've lost track of the hotel names: Canaves, Gem, Grace, Andronis, Katikies, Kapari, Kivotos. I'll let my daughter tell me which ones she likes.

journey.quote: The Veranda package at Canaves Sunday asks up to 20 guests to book two suites for at least three nights, and 21 to 40 guests require a buyout of the property under special terms.
journey.reaction: So the cheap-looking package comes with three nights of suites attached. That's exactly the hidden cost I'd want my husband to see.

journey.section: How to compare two Santorini quotes like for like
journey.quote: Canaves states that its deposit is non-refundable, that the balance is due one month before the event, and that venue payments are always non-refundable.
journey.reaction: Plain and honest. Always non-refundable. That's what I'm frightened of, and I'd rather read it here than in a contract later.

journey.section: How to compare two Santorini quotes like for like
journey.quote: **Step-free access.** Can older guests reach the ceremony and reception without stairs, and is there an accessible bathroom?
journey.reaction: Finally, someone thought of Mum. With all those cliff terraces I was waiting for this. I'm circling it before I forward the list to my husband. I'd still like to know which of these venues actually pass that test.

journey.section: How to compare two Santorini quotes like for like
journey.quote: **Currency.** What currency is the quote in, and will the deposit and balance be invoiced in the same one?
journey.reaction: Good. That's the question I'd have asked myself, and nobody else ever does.

journey.quote: The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only CNIs issued in their own country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate which applies.
journey.reaction: So for Santorini, which is it? I read it twice and it still leaves us to find out. At least it tells us who to ask.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: It notes that Greece is in an active seismic zone, including near Santorini, and that wildfires occur in the extended summer period from June to September.
journey.reaction: Honest without being alarming. I'd want to know this with older relatives coming, and it's sensible to send me to the insurer about it.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: How much does the exchange rate move the total between the deposit and the balance, and who carries that risk?
journey.reaction: Exactly the question for euros. My husband will like this one.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can book a Wedded Concierge consultation with both quotes in hand.
journey.reaction: Australian dollars and everything in writing before we commit. That's most of what I'm after. A consultation sounds like I'd get to talk to someone, which is what I want.

unanswered_questions: Which of these Santorini venues actually have step-free routes from the car to the ceremony and reception, for a guest with a walking frame?
What do 60, 70 and 80 dB mean in practice: background music only, or dancing?
For a Santorini wedding, will an Australian-issued CNI be accepted, or must it come from the embassy in Athens?
Who reads the venue contract if it is in Greek or in euros, and is the deposit protected in any way?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong on the day, at 2am Greek time?
Is the consultation a phone call with a real person before anything is booked or paid?

turn_offs_found.quote: Each includes the altar table, chandelier, lanterns with candles, Tiffany chairs, a sound system, round or rectangular tables, linen, plating, cutlery, accessible facilities, an air-conditioned bridal room, in-house catering facilities and a bar.
turn_offs_found.why: Long run-on lists like this read as a long unbroken block on an iPad. The one item that matters to me, accessible facilities, is buried in the middle where I almost missed it.

would_share_with: My husband, with the compare-quotes checklist printed and the deposit, currency and step-free access points circled
My sister, who is looking after Mum on the trip, with the seismic, wildfire and insurance paragraph
My daughter, with the Canaves room-night conditions, so she knows what the package really commits us to

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can book a Wedded Concierge consultation with both quotes in hand.
cta_reaction.why: AUD quotes and everything in writing before we commit tick my boxes. I'd click if I knew the consultation is a phone call with a named person, before anything is booked, who can tell me which venues suit my mother's mobility.

top_3_changes: Break the long inclusion lists (Santorini Gem evening packages, Andronis package) into short bullet lists so they don't read as walls of text on an iPad, and so items like 'accessible facilities' stand out.
Give the decibel limits a plain-English meaning, or simply frame them as 'ask what this allows: background music or dancing'.
Ease the roll-call of hotel names in the small-weddings section, or give each a one-line takeaway, so a careful reader doesn't lose the thread before the checklist.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, practical, reads top to bottom on an iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing business details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers treated as invisible
Title, deferred business details, sourcing and absent prices not raised as must-fix, per orchestrator
Journey types limited to the allowed enum; every turn-off has a why

open_questions.question: Step-free access is now in the checklist, which resolves this persona's main gap from Greece and Crete. Remaining asks are readability (long inclusion lists, dB limits) and are should-fix at most. Contract language, deposit protection, on-the-day contact and a phone-first step are business details and deferred.

assumptions: Margaret reads the whole article on an iPad because her daughter sent it, and her own mother uses a walking frame (per voice samples).
Prices are deliberately not printed, so their absence was not raised.
